note: WHAT THIS APP CAN AND CANNOT ANSWER ABOUT A PLACE, DECLARED. The planner is built on one rule — zones answer, circles ask — and this file is the half of that rule that has to be data. For each species group or table the app ships, it records HOW an "is this open where I am going" question is answered: by intersecting the radius with a boundary this app draws, by a row that applies statewide, by a zone row whose boundary this app does NOT draw, by a species with no dated season at all, by ocean prose, or by a water's own rules. The results screen renders this table and nothing else: a group whose boundary is absent is never asserted for a location, and the reader is sent to CDFW's zone map instead.
never_invents_rule: NOTHING IN THIS FILE IS A REGULATION AND NOTHING IN IT CHANGES ONE. A record here states where a value already in this app is read from and whether a boundary for it ships; it states no season, no date, no bag, no zone line and no limit. Every heading, caption, column, row key, season kind, species key and geometry claim below was READ off dataset/current/ when this file was written — not one was typed from memory — and pipeline/tests/test_planner_coverage.py re-derives all of them from the dataset and the geo folder and fails on drift. Delete this file and the planner loses its ability to say what it does not know; it can never change a value.

zone_geometry_layers.rule: These FIVE files are the ONLY places a zone claim may rest. They are the layers that draw a regulation's own area. A lake, an MPA, a wildlife area or a backcountry point whose NAME happens to equal a regulation's area string is not that area's boundary, and binding one to the other would be this app inventing a zone line: "Martis Creek Lake" in the waterfowl Special Management Areas table is a lake point in lakes_points.geojson, and "Morro Bay" is two MPAs and a wildlife area. Neither is the waterfowl area the table means. R40 (2026-09-19) added the fifth, CDFW's upland game zone layer, which draws the quail, band-tailed pigeon and grouse zones this file previously recorded as undrawn. R41 (2026-09-19) added the sixth, geo/text_zones.geojson, and it is the ONLY one of the six this app drew rather than read: CDFW publishes those areas as sentences and publishes no map of them, so two of them — the ones whose definition is a list of whole counties and nothing else — are assembled here from CDFW's own county polygons. Every feature in that file carries `drawn_by` saying so, and every surface that shows one prints it. An area whose definition contains one clause that is not a whole county is not in that file at all.
zone_geometry_layers.matching_rule: A table's area string finds a polygon by being that polygon's own label, character for character, or by being one of the pairs declared in curated/hunt_code_aliases_2026.json. Nothing is matched by similarity, by case folding, by prefix or by suffix. The declared pairs run in two directions and the file says which is which: `waterfowl_zone_names` is layer-spelling -> season-spelling (one-to-one), and `upland_zone_names` is row-key -> feature-id (many-to-one, because CDFW prints two Zone Q1 rows over one Q1 polygon and three grouse method rows over one grouse polygon).

zone_map_link_rule: Every `zone_map_link.url` in this file is null, and that is a finding rather than an omission: the shipped hunt tables carry CDFW's zone-map link as TEXT and not as an href. The scrape put the link text into the column heading ("Season / Area ( Zone Map (PDF )") or, for tree squirrel, into the species cell itself. So the honest link this app can offer is the CDFW page the table itself cites, recorded as `page_url` — never a FileHandler DocumentID nobody in this repository has read.
renders_rule: The results screen renders this table and nothing else. Specifically: a `statewide_row` group is answered for any location; a `zone_geometry` group is answered by intersection and names the zone; a `zone_row_without_geometry` group lists each zone's season with "this app does not draw this species' zones — see CDFW's zone map" and is never asserted for the location; a `no_dated_season` group links its own screen; an `ocean_area_prose` group shows the boundary sentence verbatim; a `water_rules` group is answered per water. Nothing else.

answered_by_vocabulary.zone_geometry: This app draws the boundary AND holds a dated season keyed on it. The planner may name the zone the radius intersects, draw it, and compute open / closed / unknown for the trip dates against that zone's own window.
answered_by_vocabulary.statewide_row: The regulation names no area smaller than the state, so the row is answered for any location inside it. The planner shows it without naming a zone, because the regulation names none.
answered_by_vocabulary.zone_row_without_geometry: The regulation divides the state into zones and this app draws none of them. The planner lists each zone's season with the honest line and CDFW's zone-map link, and NEVER asserts one of them for the reader's location. It also covers a table whose rows name no zone but whose heading links a zone map: the dates apply inside a boundary this app does not carry, so "open at your pin" would be a claim about the pin that nothing in this app can support.
answered_by_vocabulary.no_dated_season: This app holds no dated season for the group that any date engine could answer with — either the file carries no season field at all, or the only rows print "Closed", or the season ships as CDFW's printed text rather than a parsed window. The planner links the group's own free screen and says which of the three it is.
answered_by_vocabulary.ocean_area_prose: The area exists in the regulation as a sentence — a latitude line, a named point, a bay — and not as a polygon this app draws. The sentence ships verbatim, the dates ship with it, and the planner never decides whether a pin is inside the area.
answered_by_vocabulary.water_rules: Freshwater has waters, not zones. The answer is the rules published for the waters inside the radius, each with its own seasons, plus the statewide defaults. No zone is intersected because no zone exists.

groups.title: American Crow
groups.basis:
R41, 2026-09-19. THE ROW CDFW'S WEB PAGE DOES NOT PRINT. The Upland Game Birds page this table's other ten records are scraped from carries ten species tables and no crow row at all — only a link to a zone map — so until this release the app held no crow season and the planner could say nothing about crow anywhere. CDFW prints the season in its own 2026-2027 Waterfowl, Upland Game, and Lands Regulations booklet, p. 53: "American Crow / Dec 5-Apr 7 (Balance of State) / 24 / 48". That record is appended to hunt_upland.json from curated/crow_2026.json with the booklet, its page and its sha256 beside it, and its season cell goes through the same parser every scraped row goes through.

THE BOUNDARY IS CDFW'S OWN, AND IT IS THE OPEN AREA. The department draws one American Crow feature on the same Upland_Game_AGOL_gdb layer the quail, pigeon and grouse zones come from, keyed CrowOpen. R41 checked what that polygon IS rather than trusting its key: it was point-tested against § 485(d)'s two closed clauses and the answers agree on all twenty-two points tried — Alturas, Susanville, Eureka, Redding, Chester, Truckee, Bishop, Ridgecrest, Victorville, Barstow, Blythe and Hayfork are OUTSIDE it and each is inside a closed clause; Sacramento, Red Bluff, Arnold, Fresno, Bakersfield, Los Angeles, Ontario, Riverside, Escondido and Covelo are inside it and none of them is. Its northern limit is latitude 40.637, the mouth of the Eel River, which is clause (2)'s own starting point. Its own Text_in_Box lists the closed areas and ends "All other areas are open"; the polygon is those other areas.

So this group is answered exactly as every other zone_geometry group is, with no inverse reading and no new coverage kind: a radius that reaches the polygon is answered Open or Closed for the trip's days against Dec 5 - Apr 7; a radius that reaches it nowhere produces no answer and the coverage row says the radius reaches none of the zones this app draws. The one row binds to the one feature through a pair declared in curated/hunt_code_aliases_2026.json, scoped to this group — "Balance of State" is also a waterfowl zone name and is a different area, and the scope is what keeps the two apart.

NO DATE COMES FROM THE MAP LAYER, and this feature is the loudest case for that rule in the file: the layer's own Season_Dates reads "July 1 - Mar 31" and its limits read "No limit" / "No limit", against the booklet's Dec 5-Apr 7 / 24 / 48.

zone_map_link.url_basis: THE ONE ZONE-MAP HREF THIS FILE CARRIES, AND IT IS NOT A GUESS. Every other group's `url` is null because the scrape put the link's TEXT in a column heading and dropped its href. This one was read off the tracked snapshot of CDFW's own Upland Game Birds page (pipeline/snapshots/html/2026-09-19/upland.html), where the anchor is `American Crow Zone Map (PDF)`. The document behind it has been fetched, read and pinned by sha256 in this repository (pipeline/curated/crow_2026.json, slot crow_zone_map.pdf) — it is the sheet § 485(d)'s closed-area text is quoted from. It is a link this lane followed, not a DocumentID anybody composed.

citation.source_doc: CDFW 2026-2027 Waterfowl, Upland Game, and Lands Regulations, p. 53

R41, 2026-09-19 — THE TEXT IS NOW LOCATED AND QUOTED, AND THE AREAS ARE STILL NOT DRAWN. CDFW prints § 307(a) and § 307(b) beside its own Tree Squirrel Hunt Zones map sheet (nrm.dfg.ca.gov DocumentID 109005, read 2026-09-19); both are quoted verbatim in curated/text_zones_2026.json. Each one is a list of whole counties — 46 for the general season, 30 for archery and falconry — AND ONE CLAUSE THAT IS NOT: "and that portion of Kern County lying east of Interstate 5". This app holds no Interstate 5 centreline, so it cannot draw that clause, and the rule is that a county union which quietly omits part of an area is worse than no drawing at all: it would tell a hunter east of Interstate 5 in Kern County that they are outside an area the regulation puts them inside. Both areas therefore stay undrawn and the reader gets CDFW's own words. The sheet also draws a third thing — "Closed to Hunting" — which § 307 defines only by omission and never writes down. One line from a source this app may read would close this gap.

groups.title: Special Management Areas
groups.basis:
Nine sub-areas inside the zones — North Coast, Klamath Basin, Sacramento Valley, Morro Bay, the two Brant areas and the rest. CDFW draws none of them: a sweep of all 2,502 services on its ArcGIS org (R40, 2026-09-19) found no layer for any. Name collisions elsewhere in geo are not these boundaries: "Martis Creek Lake" is a lake point and "Morro Bay" is two MPAs and a wildlife area, and none of the three is the waterfowl area the table means.

R41, 2026-09-19 — ALL NINE DEFINITIONS ARE NOW QUOTED AND TWO OF THEM ARE DRAWN BY THIS APP. CDFW prints § 502(b)(6) on pp. 36-37 of the 2026-2027 Waterfowl, Upland Game, and Lands Regulations booklet; every definition is in curated/text_zones_2026.json verbatim. TWO are a list of whole counties and nothing else — North Coast ("All of Del Norte and Humboldt counties.") and Northern Brant ("Del Norte, Humboldt and Mendocino counties.") — and this app draws those two in geo/text_zones.geojson as the union of those counties in CDFW's own county layer, LABELLED AS THIS APP'S OWN LINES on every surface that shows them. The other seven are not drawn and each records the clause that stopped it: Humboldt Bay South Spit is a jetty and a mean low water line; Klamath Basin, Sacramento Valley and Imperial County are circuits of roads and highways (Imperial County is NOT the county, despite the row's name); Morro Bay is tide lines and points offshore; Martis Creek Lake is a reservoir, and the two counties in its sentence locate the lake rather than define the area; Balance of State Brant names no county at all — it is the complement of Northern Brant, and a complement drawn from county polygons that stop at the shoreline would tell a brant hunter on the water they are in no area.

THE GROUP STAYS `zone_row_without_geometry` BECAUSE SEVEN OF THE NINE ROWS ARE STILL UNDRAWN. Coverage flips only when every zone row in a group is drawable. What changes for a reader is per row: the two drawn rows are answered against their drawn area when the radius reaches it, with the sentence saying who drew the line; the other seven behave exactly as before.

zone_geometry.note: `exists` stays false because the GROUP is not zone-backed: seven of its nine rows are undrawn. Two rows do reach a drawn area and they are declared in `text_zone_rows`, not here — a row-level drawing is not a group-level one, and folding it in would let a reader of this table believe the nine areas were mapped.
